title:
UN Court Finds Myanmar Committed Genocide.
Israeli Tanks Cross Gaza's Yellow Line.
Kenya's Marathon Star Banned.
subject: UN Court Finds Myanmar Committed Genocide. Israeli Tanks Cross Gaza's Yellow Line. Kenya's Marathon Star Banned.
preview_text: A landmark Rohingya verdict, a Gaza incursion, a doping ban, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: The ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, Israeli forces push past Gaza's Yellow Line and Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir gets a doping ban.
contents_extra: Asia's neighbours at the Apec summit, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: UN Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya
paragraphs: The BBC reports the International Court of Justice found Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. The judges ruled nine votes to six on that finding. It is the first time an international court has found a state guilty of genocide. Judge Iwasawa Yuji said Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya.

By 11 votes to four, the court found Myanmar failed in its duty to punish genocide. It said Myanmar must make reparations, with the amount set at a later stage. Myanmar had denied genocide and said its forces were responding to attacks by armed groups. The Guardian reported fears before the ruling that the US could sanction ICJ judges.

stories.title: Israeli Tanks Push Past Gaza's Yellow Line Near Nuseirat
paragraphs: The BBC reports Israeli ground forces launched a rare operation in central Gaza outside their control. Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp under artillery cover. The Israeli military said the targeted operation aimed to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line. That line marks the more than 60% of Gaza that Israel occupies.

The Guardian reports it was the first ground operation across the line since the October 2025 ceasefire. Dozens of displaced Palestinians fled their tents, the paper says. Hamas called the raid a flagrant violation of the ceasefire. The move came a day after the US-backed Board of Peace accused both sides of failing to honour their commitments.

stories.title: Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir Gets a Three-Year Doping Ban
paragraphs: BBC Sport reports world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for using EPO. An out-of-competition sample was collected in Kenya before she won the Sydney Marathon on Aug. 30. She denied using EPO but signed an admission form. She is one of three high-profile Kenyan athletes sanctioned.

The Guardian reports her ban was reduced by a year after she chose not to challenge the test result. She has been stripped of her Sydney win. BBC Sport says Veronica Loleo also received a three-year ban. Ronald Korir got six years after failing to explain abnormalities in his biological passport.

deep_dive.title: Inside the Apec Summit, Asia's Neighbours Get Mixed Signals From China
paragraphs: Reuters reports Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday to stand up against trade protectionism. He spoke at the Apec summit in Shenzhen. His speech followed new US curbs on China's access to AI chips. Reuters also reports that smaller countries fear great-power deals may sideline them. The summit brings together leaders from 21 member economies.

CNBC reports South Korean entertainment and travel stocks surged Thursday after Seoul and Beijing largely concluded a trade deal. Seoul's trade ministry said China offered most-favored-nation treatment to Korean industries including films and games. Studio Dragon soared 29.96%, while CJ ENM jumped 26%. NH Investment & Securities said the deal does not explicitly lift curbs on K-pop concerts.

The Guardian reports Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a modest welcome in Shenzhen. She was greeted by a relatively junior Chinese official, the paper says. Other leaders got military bands and bouquets. The Guardian links the contrast to a simmering row over Taiwan. It is her first visit to China since taking office just over a year ago.

CNBC reports a South China Sea code of conduct missed its 2026 deadline at the Asean summit in the Philippines. Manila reported that 80% of the negotiating text was complete. Talks are set to continue under next Asean chair Singapore. Experts quoted by CNBC are skeptical that an effective code can be agreed in the short term.

trivia.question: How many years after it sank was the wreck of HMCS Spitfire, Australia's first locally built warship, discovered?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 128. The Guardian reports marine archaeologists found the wreck off far north Queensland.

poll.question: Should international courts be able to rule that a state committed genocide?

Russia questions the Netherlands over a bridge strike, The Guardian reports Dutch-based Destinus said its missiles were used in the Kerch bridge attack.

Musk says he regrets his midterm spending, CNBC reports he said he felt pretty foolish about spending at least $474 million.

A top scientist warns over IPCC delays, The Guardian reports Johan Rockstrom said slowing the work puts cooperation at risk.

Hamilton denies a trust problem at Ferrari, The Guardian reports he spoke before the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Life & culture: African stars feature in GTA 6, The BBC reports DJ Lag, Burna Boy and Asake are on the soundtrack.
Syria's women's football starts to recover, The Guardian reports the civil war had ground the women's game to a halt.
A zoo hippo is treated after swallowing a hat, The BBC reports Fiona is under emergency care at Cincinnati Zoo.
